features.title: One pill. Four instincts.
features.lead: TapCopy reads what you selected and shows only the segments that make sense. No shortcuts to memorize, no window stealing your focus.
features.detectBody: Links get Open. Real file paths get Show in Finder. #10B981 turns into rgb(16, 185, 129) with a live swatch. (49 * 12) - 88 resolves to = 500 on the spot.
features.detectNote: Dates and phone numbers are ignored: 2026-11-14 is never treated as a subtraction.
features.plainBody: Plain copies clean text without formatting. Aa converts to UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, snake_case, camelCase or a Markdown code block, with a live word and character count.
features.searchBody: The magnifier searches the web instantly. When the selection looks like code, the menu adds GitHub code search and Stack Overflow.
features.pinBody: Pin up to 4 draggable cards on screen, Dropover-style. Copy them again later and close them when you're done. The fifth pin replaces the oldest.
features.overlapBody: TapCopy reads the macOS Accessibility tree and floating windows before it appears, so it never covers web buttons like “Ask Gemini”, Notion bars, Medium or ChatGPT toolbars. Six candidate slots are scored every time.
features.lightBody: Swift 5.10 and pure AppKit. Under 1 MB, 0.0% CPU at rest, built for macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Selecting text never writes to your clipboard.

tutorial.title: From install to your first pill.
tutorial.lead: Watch the walkthrough: Accessibility permission, Chameleon Mode and the Pin Shelf.
tutorial.privacyNote: The video loads from youtube-nocookie.com only after you press play.
tutorial.step1Body: TapCopy lives in your menu bar. Drag it from the .dmg to Applications and open it.
tutorial.step2Body: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility. The menu-bar icon switches from a warning triangle to the clipboard silhouette.
tutorial.step3Body: Drag over text, double-click a word or Shift-click to extend. Click a segment. The pill hides after 5 seconds, or instantly with Esc.

privacy: This policy explains how BLACK EYE (“we”) handles information related to TapCopy, the macOS app, and its website tapcopy.iareal.net.

TapCopy reads the text you select through the macOS Accessibility API to show the Chameleon Pill. Your selected text is processed 100% locally on your Mac and is never uploaded, stored or transmitted — not for telemetry, not for analytics, not for training. The only network requests TapCopy ever makes are license activation or deactivation and the signed update check, both to tapcopy.iareal.net.

TapCopy asks for the Accessibility permission only. It does not ask for Screen Recording. When you click Open or Search, TapCopy hands the link or query to your default browser; what happens next is governed by that website's own policy.

You can download the 14-day trial without providing any data. If you choose to enter an email address, we use it only to send information related to your trial and TapCopy. When you buy a license, our payment provider processes your payment details; we receive the information needed to issue and validate your license (such as email, plan and license key). We do not store full card numbers.

The website stores one functional cookie, tapcopy-lang, for one year, only when you choose a language manually. To show the right language on your first visit, our hosting provider passes us your approximate country and your browser's language preference; we do not store them. The site loads fonts from Google Fonts. The tutorial video loads from youtube-nocookie.com only after you press play. The WhatsApp button opens WhatsApp, which is governed by Meta's own policies.
You can ask us to access, correct or delete the email or license information we hold about you. Write to tapcopy@iareal.net.
If we update this policy, we will change the date at the top of this page.
